subject: Post-call: Finex throughput & SLOs
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Smith <jordan@finex-analytics.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-call: Finex throughput & SLOs

Thanks for the call earlier today — good to meet the Finex team. Quick recap and the follow-ups we agreed on so we have a shared record. Please flag anything I missed.

Call highlights / clarified requirements:
- Primary workload: real-time enrichment & summarization for user chat sessions. Typical customer session: ~80 input tokens, ~256 output tokens (avg).
- Latency targets (customer preference): p50 <= 200ms, p95 <= 450ms for 256-token completions.
- Streaming: token-by-token streaming required for the UI; start-of-stream target <= 120ms, sustained token emission >= 25 tokens/sec.
- Throughput & concurrency:
  - Steady-state: ~15 req/s (QPS) across US region.
  - Peak bursts: up to ~120 req/s for short periods (~20-60s) during load spikes (8x peak/steady).
  - Expected concurrent active sessions during peak: ~300 concurrent short-lived streams.
- Workload shape: traffic is spiky (hourly bursts) with tail-heavy outputs during certain workflows (reports).

Preliminary sizing ask (what we will validate next):
- Peak tokens/sec (estimated): ~120 req/s * 256 tokens = ~30,700 outbound tokens/sec (+ inputs) => plan for ~35k tokens/sec headroom.
- Sustained tokens/sec (steady): 15 req/s * 256 = ~3,840 tokens/sec.

Action items / next steps:
1) Finex: share a 24h sample of anonymized request logs (timestamps, input token counts, output token counts, % streaming vs non-streaming). Jordan, can you send this by EOD Monday?
2) Redwood: we'll provision a short benchmark window using a dedicated test pool and run a 2-hour peak/steady benchmark. Marissa will own the runbook and will need an allowlist IP + API key from Finex.
3) Redwood: deliver a sizing worksheet (tokens/sec, target QPS, recommended instance types, expected p50/p95 ranges) and a benchmark plan.
4) Finex: confirm whether p95 latency goal is a hard SLO or a target for the team to optimize toward.

Attachments referenced: finex-slo-summary.xlsx (we'll attach a one-page summary with our initial assumptions).

Thanks — Rafael
--
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rafael@redwood.ai

From: Jordan Smith <jordan@finex-analytics.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 15:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Finex throughput & SLOs

Thanks Rafael — great summary and yes, this matches what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Latency SLOs: p50 <= 150ms would be ideal for our real-time product path; p95 <= 500ms is acceptable for now. We understand there is a tradeoff when optimizing for throughput.
- Streaming: start-of-stream <= 100ms if possible; sustained emission of 25-30 tokens/sec is fine.
- Concurrency: our earlier note on 300 concurrent streams during peak is on the higher side for the pilot; for the initial rollout assume ~150 concurrent sessions, but the system must be able to handle spikes up to 300.
- Test data: we'll sanitize and send a 24-hour sample by Monday (as requested). We'll include per-request token counts and a histogram of request inter-arrival times.

Questions for Redwood: 
1) When you run the benchmark, are you able to validate streaming start latency separately from end-to-end completion latency? We want separate metrics for both.
2) For the sizing worksheet, please include recommended quantization / model variants if there is a big perf/cost tradeoff we should consider.

Jordan
Jordan Smith
Senior Product Manager, Finex Analytics
jordan@finex-analytics.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Great — thanks for the clarifications, Jordan. Rafael and I will prep the benchmark plan and the sizing worksheet. Quick notes on logistics: 

- I'll attach the benchmark plan + SLO summary (finex-benchmark-plan.pdf, finex-slo-summary.xlsx) and share a Drive link.
- Rafael: I'll need the allowlist IP ranges (Finex infra) and the API key scope you'd like used for the test environment. Jordan, if possible please provide the sanitized sample and an allowlist entry by Monday so we can schedule the run for next Thursday (2026-08-27) 16:00-18:00 PT.
- During the run we'll collect: start-of-stream latency distribution, per-token emission latency, p50/p95/p99 for completions, and tokens/sec observed.

I'll follow up with a calendar invite for the benchmark window once we confirm your allowlist and the sample.

Thanks — Marissa
